claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

=== YOUR SITUATION PROFILE ===
You live in the UK.
You are inquiring about your 1 child:
  - Alex is 8 years old and lives with you.

Here are the exact details of your circumstances to use when answering the agent's questions:

Regarding Alex:
  - Claimant lives in the UK
  - Child is 8 (under 16)
  - Child lives with claimant
  - Child in local authority care for 12 weeks (>8) and does not spend 24+ hours/week at home
  - Child is not in hospital or residential accommodation
  - Child is not fostered
  - Child does not work 24+ hours/week
  - Child has not started an apprenticeship in England
  - Child does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right

expected_eligibility.name: Alex
expected_eligibility.reason: Child in local authority care for 12 weeks (>8) and does not spend 24+ hours/week at home
circumstances: Child in local authority care for 12 weeks (>8) and does not spend 24+ hours/week at home
Child is not in hospital or residential accommodation

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit! Let me start the assessment by getting the first question.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To get started, I need to know about your child or children. 

**How old is each child you're claiming Child Benefit for?** Please tell me:
- The child's name
- Their date of birth (or current age)

Once I know their age, I can guide you through the eligibility requirements. The age of your child is important because different rules apply at different ages:
- **Under 16**: Generally qualify automatically
- **16-19**: Must meet certain education or training requirements
- **20 or older**: Generally don't qualify

Could you tell me about your child/children?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes, I'm interested in finding out if I can claim Child Benefit. I have one child, Alex, who's 8 years old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Thank you for that information. Alex is 8 years old, which means he falls into the **under 16 category**. This is good news as children under 16 generally qualify automatically for Child Benefit.

However, I need to check a few more things to complete the eligibility assessment. Let me move forward with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question: Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week (or not in any paid work)?**

This is a requirement to check - children who work 24+ hours per week while not in approved education or training may not be eligible. Since Alex is only 8 years old, I assume he's not in paid work, but I need to confirm this for the assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't work at all. He's only 8, so he's just in primary school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That's what I expected - Alex is in primary school and not working, so that requirement is met. Let me continue with the next eligibility check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question: Is Alex NOT receiving certain benefits in his own right?**

Specifically, I need to check if Alex is receiving:
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA), or
- Universal Credit in his own right

Since Alex is only 8 years old and in primary school, he shouldn't be receiving these, but I need to confirm this for the eligibility check.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't receive any benefits in his own name. He's just a young child, so nothing like that.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's clear - Alex isn't receiving any of those benefits. Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question: Is Alex NOT in a disqualifying apprenticeship?**

This is mainly relevant for older children/young people. Since Alex is only 8 years old and in primary school, he's definitely not in any apprenticeship. 

Can you confirm that Alex is not in any apprenticeship scheme (approved or otherwise)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's right, Alex isn't in any apprenticeship. He's only 8, so he's just doing regular primary school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! That's clear - Alex is not in any apprenticeship. Now let me move to the next important check regarding your residency situation.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Now I need to check your residency situation.**

This is an important requirement for Child Benefit eligibility. There are several ways you can meet the residency requirement. Let me ask you about your situation:

**Do you normally live in the UK?** 

Or if you don't normally live in the UK, do you have any of the following:
- Settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme
- Pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme (with certain conditions about work, job-seeking, studying, or resources)
- Are you a Crown servant living abroad

Which of these applies to your situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I normally live in the UK. We live here in England.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! You meet the residency requirement - you normally live in the UK in England. Let me move forward to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question: Are you responsible for Alex?**

Responsibility for a child means either:
1. **Living with the child** - You live with them in your home, OR
2. **Contributing to their upkeep** - You pay at least the equivalent of Child Benefit (or more) towards their care, which could include food, clothes, pocket money, housing, presents, etc.
3. **Paying maintenance** - You're paying maintenance under a court order or agreement

Which of these applies to your situation with Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex lives with me at home.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! You live with Alex - that clearly establishes your responsibility for him. Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question: Is anyone else claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

This is important because only one person can claim Child Benefit for each child. 

Is there:
- **No other person** claiming for Alex, OR
- **Another person claiming** but you've both agreed who should claim, OR
- **A disputed situation** where you and another person can't agree who should claim?

Which applies to your situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! That's clear - you're the only person claiming for Alex. Let me proceed to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question: Where is Alex living?**

I need to check if any special circumstances apply:

- **In hospital** - Being treated as an inpatient
- **In care** - In local authority care
- **Fostered** - In a fostering arrangement
- **Living normally** - At home with you as usual

Which applies to Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex has been in local authority care for a few months now.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that important information. Since Alex is in local authority care, I need to check how long he's been in that situation, as this affects eligibility.

Let me get the details about the duration rules.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Important question about Alex's care arrangement:**

When a child is in local authority care, there are special rules about Child Benefit eligibility:

- You can continue claiming for up to **8 weeks** after the child enters care
- **Exception**: If the child spends at least **24 hours per week at home** (with you), you can continue claiming even after 8 weeks
- You can claim again if the child spends **2 consecutive nights per week OR 7+ days in a row** at home

Given that Alex has been in care for a few months (longer than 8 weeks), I need to know:

**Does Alex spend at least 24 hours per week at home with you?** (This could be spread across multiple visits - for example, 3-4 hours several times a week, or overnight stays)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't come home that much. He's at the care home full-time.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. Unfortunately, this means Alex doesn't meet the exception criteria. Since Alex has been in local authority care for a few months (which is longer than 8 weeks) and doesn't spend at least 24 hours per week at home with you, I'm afraid you would not be eligible to claim Child Benefit for him.

Let me navigate to confirm this outcome.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm sorry to inform you that based on your circumstances, **you are not eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex**.

**Here's why:**

Child Benefit eligibility has special rules when a child is in local authority care:
- You can continue claiming for the first **8 weeks** after the child enters care
- After that, you can only continue claiming if the child spends at least **24 hours per week at home** with you
- Since Alex has been in care for several months (longer than 8 weeks) AND doesn't spend at least 24 hours per week at home, the eligibility requirement is not met

**However, there is a potential path back to eligibility:**

If the care arrangement changes in the future and Alex spends at least:
- **2 consecutive nights each week at home**, OR
- **7+ consecutive days in a row at home**

Then you would be able to claim Child Benefit again. You would need to contact HMRC to restart your claim at that point.

**What you should do:**
- Contact HMRC to inform them of Alex's current care status if you haven't already done so
- Keep your details updated with HMRC so you can claim again if circumstances change
- Reference: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit-for-children-in-hospital-or-care

Is there anything else I can help clarify about this situation, or do you have any other questions?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
I understand. Thank you for explaining that to me. It's disappointing, but I appreciate you walking me through all the details and letting me know what the situation is.

<function_calls>
<invoke name="exit_loop">
</invoke>
</function_calls>

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
You're very welcome. I'm glad I could help you understand the situation clearly, even though it's not the outcome you were hoping for.

To summarize what we found:
- **Alex meets most eligibility criteria** - he's under 16, not working, not receiving benefits, not in an apprenticeship, you live in the UK, you're responsible for him, and no one else is claiming for him
- **The issue is the care arrangement** - because Alex has been in local authority care for more than 8 weeks and doesn't spend at least 24 hours per week at home, Child Benefit eligibility is paused

The good news is that this isn't necessarily permanent. If Alex's care situation changes and he spends more time at home with you (at least 2 consecutive nights per week or 7+ days in a row), you can reclaim Child Benefit.

**Please do contact HMRC** to:
1. Make sure they have the current information about Alex's care status
2. Ask about any other support or benefits you might be eligible for during this period
3. Understand what steps to take if the arrangement changes

You can reach HMRC at:
- **Phone**: 0300 200 3100
- **Website**: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit

I'm sorry I couldn't bring better news, but I hope this explanation has been helpful. If you have any other questions in the future, feel free to ask. Best of luck with your situation.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Thank you so much for your help and for being so thorough. I really appreciate it.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
You're very welcome! I'm really glad I could help you understand your situation thoroughly. It's important to have clarity on these things, even when the outcome isn't what you hoped for.

If circumstances change or if you have any other questions about Child Benefit eligibility in the future, please don't hesitate to reach out. I'm here to help.

Wishing you and Alex all the best. Take care! 🙂

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
Thank you, take care!

<function_calls>
<invoke name="exit_loop">
</invoke>
</function_calls>

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: You're welcome! Take care! 👋
